problems.stem: A teacher wants to add a daily five-minute entry routine using a polling app. Which justification makes the routine defensible rather than tool-driven?
options: The app shows a live bar chart, so the class will find it fun.
The poll surfaces yesterday's most common error so the teacher can open with a targeted re-teach.
Every student has a district device, so the routine will run smoothly.
The app can timestamp responses for the gradebook.
problems.explanation: The defensible version names the learning move the routine serves (diagnosing and re-teaching a common error). The other options justify the routine by tool features or smooth operation.

problems.stem: After running a gamified review routine, a teacher writes in the Tension Studio map: "Students loved it, leaderboard was packed." What is the strongest reason this is not yet evidence that the routine should stay?
options: Leaderboards are never appropriate in a classroom.
Enthusiasm and on-task behavior do not show whether the targeted concept was learned.
The note is too short to count as a portfolio entry.
The teacher should have used a different app.
problems.explanation: Engagement is necessary but not sufficient. The map needs a learning check or artifact, not just evidence of attention, to justify keeping the routine.

problems.stem: A teacher asks TeachGen@i to design a tech-rich opening routine. The draft assumes every student logs in from a personal device at home the night before. What is the most defensible teacher move?
options: Adopt the routine as written because the AI optimized it for engagement.
Reject the home-login assumption and add an in-class, non-device fallback so a student without home access still completes the learning move.
Remove the routine entirely because AI cannot plan equitable routines.
Keep the assumption but tell students to use the library before school.
problems.explanation: The teacher names who the routine excludes when access fails and builds a fallback that preserves the learning move, treating the AI draft as a proposal rather than authority.

problems.stem: On the Design Tension Studio map for a new tech-rich routine, which paired entry best documents a defensible decision a mentor could audit?
options: "Routine is engaging" paired with "students like the app."
Tension named (instructional time vs. device setup) paired with the negotiated decision (move setup to the prior afternoon so the routine reclaims four minutes of instruction).
"Followed the lesson plan" paired with "no complaints."
problems.explanation: A defensible map pairs a named value tension with the negotiated decision and its consequence, which is exactly what a mentor can inspect and question.
